Cyber Attack Disrupts Saudi Hospitality Sector, Forcing Hotel Closures and Guest Evacuations

A significant cyber attack has struck several major hospitality firms in Saudi Arabia, disrupting operations across the sector and forcing the temporary closure of dozens of hotels and resorts in Riyadh, Jeddah, and the Eastern Province. The attack, which began in the early hours of Tuesday, targeted IT systems with what sources describe as a sophisticated ransomware campaign, paralyzing reservation platforms and electronic access controls.

The Saudi Hospitality Group Association confirmed that multiple member firms, including Al Waha Resorts and Palm Crescent Hotels, have reported severe operational outages. "Our members are facing unprecedented challenges to guest safety and service continuity," said association spokesperson Maha Al-Qahtani. "Many properties have had to evacuate guests as a precaution, given the loss of access to digital control systems."

The attack has left front desk and back office systems inoperable, with staff reverting to manual processes where possible. At the Al Waha Resort in Jeddah, hotel manager Faisal Al-Mutairi described the situation as "extremely challenging," noting that "without access to digital room keys and management systems, we had no choice but to temporarily close and assist guests in finding alternative accommodation."

Industry analysts estimate that more than 60 hotels and serviced apartments have been affected as of Wednesday afternoon. The disruption has resulted in the cancellation of thousands of bookings, with immediate economic losses likely to run into the tens of millions of riyals. "The impact on both revenue and industry confidence is severe," said hospitality analyst Lina Al-Dossary. "The sector relies heavily on digital platforms for everything from bookings to guest services."

Hospitality sector workers have also been impacted, with many unable to report for shifts or perform duties due to system outages. The National Hospitality Workers Federation reported that over 4,000 staff are currently sidelined. "We are working closely with employers to ensure wage protections during this crisis," said federation chairperson Saleh Al-Omari.

Authorities and affected companies are working to restore operations, though no timeline for resolution has yet been provided.
